items.title: Mozambique: Cabinet approves 2026-27 Contingency Plan budgeted at 39.8 billion meticais — AIM report

items.title: Mozambique and Qatar interested in strengthening cooperation in labour
items.summary: Maputo, 04 Nov (AIM) – The governments of Mozambique and Qatar have expressed interest in strengthening economic and labour cooperation, including the recruitment of Mozambican workers to the Gulf country. According to Maria Manso Mozambican minister of Foreign Affairs – who was speaking at the end of the second round of political consultations between the two countries, held during the visit of Ahmed bin Hassan Al Hammadi, Qatari Secretary-General of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, to Mozambique – the focus is on expanding the cooperation at various levels. “Economic cooperation is our calling card, in this case, for strengthening these relations. At this stage, we want to strengthen our foundation, which is the signing of our general cooperation agreement. This will be the driving force behind the implementation of all the other cooperation initiatives we will undertake”, she said. Manso also said that the parties discussed and identified several areas with potential for joint development.

items.title: Rwanda's army team removed from Africa league after US sanctions, NBA says
items.summary: Rwanda's army team APR came third in the Basketball Africa League last year The National Basketball Association (NBA) says it removed Rwanda's army team from its African league because of US sanctions imposed on the country in March The NBA had previously said the Rwandan army-funded Armée Patriotique Rwandaise (APR) club would not participate in the 2026 Basketball Africa League (BAL) However this is the first time the NBA has revealed the reasons behind the APR's removal The association was responding to complaints by two US senators, who sent a letter asking them to reconsider their partnership with the Rwandan team. The US placed sanctions on the Rwandan army, accusing it of fuelling the conflict in the Democratic Republic of Congo in March The senators said the NBA risked "becoming complicit in sportswashing by accepting money from a Rwandan government that systematically abuses human rights" Last week, the US also imposed sanctions on Rwanda's defence ministry over its support for the M23 rebel group which has seized control of large parts of eastern DR Congo.

items.title: Germany's celebrated children's author Janosch has died
items.summary: Bear, Tiger and Tiger-Duck: The author and illustrator Janosch achieved world fame with his heartwarming children's figures. He died at the age of 95 Janosch, the pen name of German author and illustrator Horst Eckert, won hearts around the world with his warm and simple sense of humor. He charmed children and adults alike with his iconic Tiger, Bear, Tiger-Duck and other animals Janosch created more than 150 books , which have been translated into over 30 languages His best-selling children's book, "Oh, wie schön ist Panama," translated into English as "The Trip to Panama," was so lucrative that Janosch was able to settle down on the Canary Island of Tenerife in 1980, where he lived together with his wife Ines. The writer and illustrator died peacefully at the age of 95, his publisher Bernhard Feil announced on Wednesday Janosch was born as Horst Eckert on March 11, 1931, in Hindenburg (now Zabrze, Poland) in what was then Upper Silesia.

items.title: Iran's chief negotiator says Americans voted 'no to war'
items.summary: Mohammed Bagher Ghalibaf said Iran "endorsed" the message sent by American voters Iran's chief negotiator in talks with the US has said that Americans have "said NO TO WAR", after President Donald Trump's Republican Party suffered a stunning defeat in the midterm elections "We endorse this message," parliament speaker Mohammed Bagher Ghalibaf wrote on X "If the US [government] betrays their public will to serve international paymasters and blackmailers, it will learn our NO comes with a Nightmare," he warned Trump acknowledged on Tuesday that the poor results for Republican congressional candidates were partly due to the war and the related surge in petrol prices.

items.title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline
items.summary: More than 500 parties are contesting the elections South Africans are voting in highly contested local elections likely to see a haemorrhaging of votes for the country's biggest party, the African National Congress (ANC) This year's voting season has been marked by intense campaigns that have included politicians spinning cars, watching grannies knit and even wading through giant-sized potholes Leaders are campaigning to head South Africa's nearly 300 municipalities, responsible for basic service provision such as water, electricity and refuse collection For the ANC, the elections are a chance to prove it still has what it takes to govern. The party had a disastrous showing in the last national election, when it lost its parliamentary majority for the first time since 1994 when the racist apartheid system ended Support for the party has been dropping significantly over the years because of anger over high levels of corruption, unemployment and crime At its peak, in 2004, the ANC got 70% of the vote in the general election.

items.title: How America voted in maps and charts
items.summary: It's been an extraordinary night for the Democrats in the US midterms They have taken control of the Senate and the House of Representatives too The results in the Senate are beyond what the Democrats would have expected. North Carolina was a likely pick-up but South Carolina was a huge shock and Kansas had not returned a Democratic senator since 1932 Texas , Iowa , Ohio and Maine have also turned blue and the Democrats held Michigan . There is one toss-up seat to come in Alaska and even Mississippi is now on a knife edge, according to CBS News Polls before the election saw South Carolina as leaning Republican. It had been a deep red seat for many years, last returning a Democratic senator in 1998 The shift from Republican to Democrat happened across the country.
